culture-cycles.note: Bank holidays notified for the RBI Thiruvananthapuram office for 2026; state government offices usually close on these days too, but the state's own gazette list can differ. Where RBI shows several festival names for one day, the label lists all of them; the one that applies here is the festival observed in this state. Dates before 5 November 2026 have passed; replace with the 2027 list when RBI publishes it. Lunar and Islamic dates move each year.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Most temples accept saree, churidar, long skirt and blouse or modest modern outfits for women. In most temples men are expected to enter bare-chested with a dhoti, shoulders uncovered. Visitors are asked to avoid non-vegetarian food, bathe and wear fresh clothes on the day of a visit.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Circumambulate the sanctum as the particular temple prescribes, usually clockwise; at some Shiva temples you stop at a set point and retrace your steps rather than completing the circuit.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Kerala Tourism (Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala); individual temple authorities.
culture-and-protocol.note: Temple customs only, from Kerala Tourism's FAQ. Entry rules for non-Hindus vary by temple and are not stated on this page.

laws.rule: Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance prohibits consuming alcohol in its forest and ecotourism areas.
Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance prohibits smoking in its forest and ecotourism areas.
Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance prohibits drug use in its forest and ecotourism areas.
Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance says pets are not allowed in its forest and ecotourism areas; do not collect plants or animals.
Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance says not to feed fish or other wild animals, disturb wildlife, or discard food and litter on land or into water.
Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance says visitors should not remain in parks or reserves between 7 pm and 7 am unless accommodation is provided. Confirm the rules at the particular site.
Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance says visitors should carry government-authorised identity proof and produce it when required, and follow the instructions of guides and forest personnel.
Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance says not to carry weapons and to avoid loud noise, music and horns in its forest and ecotourism areas.
Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance says travelling alone in the forests is prohibited and asks visitors to seek a guide; ask the programme about the intended route and group.

Kerala Forest Department ecotourism guidance asks visitors to consider consent before photographing people and to respect local customs. This is the department guidance, not a claim to speak for individual communities.

layers.process: The Kerala Forest Department ecotourism programme asks visitors to obtain any necessary permission before visiting. Its booking portal lists destinations including Eravikulam, Thekkady/Periyar East and Chinnar. Ask the named site whether the specific activity needs a permit or booking, and confirm opening and availability before travelling.
